case.title: Will the FOMC leave the target range for the federal funds rate unchanged at its October 27-28, 2026 meeting?
case.resolution_rule: YES if the policy statement released by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) at the end of its scheduled meeting of October 27-28, 2026, as published on federalreserve.gov, keeps both the lower bound and the upper bound of the target range for the federal funds rate equal to the target range in effect immediately before that meeting. NO if either bound is changed (a cut or an increase of any size). Cut, hold and increase are mutually exclusive outcomes of one decision; they are scored as this single yes/no question, not as separate events.

evidence.title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement (September 16, 2026; full statement text)
evidence.content:
The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 12 – 0 vote:

The Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate. The Committee is continuing its policy of maintaining ample reserves in the banking system.

Economic activity is expanding at a solid pace. While uncertainty remains elevated owing, in part, to geopolitical developments, domestic spending has been resilient. Productivity growth is strong, and capital investment is robust. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little.

Inflation remains elevated. Today's policy action will support a timelier return to the Committee's 2 percent goal. The Committee will deliver price stability.

evidence.title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee, September 15-16, 2026 (verbatim excerpt: paragraphs containing 'outlook for monetary policy')
evidence.content: With regard to the outlook for monetary policy beyond the current meeting, most participants assessed that another increase in the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate by year end. Participants emphasized, however, that they approached each meeting with an open mind and decisions at future meetings would depend on incoming information and its implications for the outlook and the balance of risks.

evidence.title: BLS news release: Consumer Price Index - September 2026 (verbatim excerpt: opening summary paragraphs)
evidence.content:
CONSUMER PRICE INDEX - SEPTEMBER 2026

The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) increased 0.6 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in September after rising 0.4 percent in August, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today. Over the last 12 months, the all items index increased 3.7 percent before seasonal adjustment.

The index for gasoline rose 9.1 percent in September, accounting for over half of the monthly all items increase. The energy index increased 5.2 percent over the month following a 2.1-percent increase in August. The shelter index rose 0.4 percent in September after rising 0.3 percent in August. The index for food was unchanged in September, as the index for food away from home increased 0.2 percent and the index for food at home fell 0.1 percent.

The index for all items less food and energy rose 0.3 percent in September, as it did in August. Indexes that increased over the month include recreation, used cars and trucks, education, airline fares, medical care, and apparel. Conversely, the index for communication was among the small number of major indexes that decreased in September.

The all items index rose 3.7 percent for the 12 months ending September, a larger increase than the 3.4-percent increase reported for the 12 months ending in August. The all items less food and energy index rose 2.6 percent over the year, following a 2.4-percent increase over the 12 months ending August. The energy index increased 20.4 percent for the 12 months ending September. The food index increased 2.5 percent over the last year.

evidence.title: BLS news release: The Employment Situation - September 2026 (verbatim excerpt: opening summary paragraph)
evidence.content:
THE EMPLOYMENT SITUATION - SEPTEMBER 2026

Both nonfarm payroll employment (+29,000) and the unemployment rate (4.2 percent) changed little in September, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today. Employment in all major industries changed little over the month.

curation_notes.selection: docs/CASES.md Part 1, rules 1-9 (pre-registered before this file was built)
curation_notes.as_of_rule: 00:00:00 UTC, 7 calendar days before the statement release date
curation_notes.contamination: Default replay model llama3.1:8b: knowledge cutoff December 2023 (Meta model card). This 2026 event is after that cutoff, so contamination_flag = unlikely (never 'none'). Check any other model's card first. The curator (Claude, training data to about mid-2026) may itself know the answer; the mechanical rule is what stops that from steering case or evidence choice.

evidence_classification.fomc-2026-oct.statement: Official FOMC policy statement. documentary_fact: the policy action and vote it records; analyst_interpretation: the Committee's own description of the economy and its forward guidance (official guidance, not a numeric forecast).
evidence_classification.fomc-2026-oct.minutes: Official minutes, verbatim excerpt. analyst_interpretation: summarized views of FOMC participants on the outlook for policy, as written by the FOMC Secretariat (not individual quotes, not a numeric forecast).
evidence_classification.fomc-2026-oct.cpi: Official BLS statistical release, verbatim excerpt. documentary_fact: measured price changes as first published (later revisions are not reflected).
evidence_classification.fomc-2026-oct.jobs: Official BLS statistical release, verbatim excerpt. documentary_fact: survey estimates as first published (subject to later revision).

curation_notes.excerpt_method: Verbatim. Fed pages fetched live on observed_at; HTML tags removed, entities decoded, runs of whitespace collapsed to one space, paragraphs joined with a blank line; non-breaking hyphens kept. Each paragraph was also found verbatim (whitespace-normalized) in the archive_url capture, which is dated before as_of. BLS pages refuse automated requests (HTTP 403), so BLS text is taken from the archive_url capture (before as_of) of the permanent BLS archive URL; each excerpt paragraph was also found in a second pre-as_of capture of the BLS current-release page. Preformatted line breaks were joined with spaces.
curation_notes.release_times: FOMC statements and minutes: 'For release at 2:00 p.m. EDT' on the press release (18:00 UTC). BLS: 'embargoed until 8:30 a.m. (ET)' on the release (12:30 UTC, daylight time). published_at = available_at = that release time.

market.venue_rule_differences: Kalshi YES = 'a Hike of 0bps'. Polymarket measures the change in the upper bound only. This case requires both bounds unchanged. The FOMC sets both bounds together, so these agree unless a bound moves alone. Cancelled meeting: Kalshi (markets after the May 2025 meeting): a cancelled scheduled meeting counts as 'Fed maintains rate'; Polymarket resolves 'No change' if no statement is released by the end of the next scheduled meeting (docs/CANDIDATE_MARKETS.md, 'FOMC rule edge cases'; rule text checked by #66, not re-read here).
